Estimate which month the snapshot describes. Use only the figures supplied plus your general knowledge of economic history.

text:
This looks like April 2018. The unemployment rate of 4.1%, the fed funds rate of 1.70%, the 10-year yield of 2.96% and the 2-year yield of 2.49% all fit that month.

Several other readings point the same way:
- US large-cap equity fell 6.7% over 3 months, which matches the Q1 2018 selloff after the January peak.
- The broad dollar was down 5.1% year over year, consistent with the weak dollar of 2017.
- The 10-year yield first approached 3% in April 2018, and the 2-year was about 2.5%.
- Fed funds at 1.70% fits an effective rate of about 1.69% in April 2018, after the March hike.

The 1-month US equity return of +0.5% fits April 2018 (S&P 500 +0.4%). March 2018 was -2.5%, so the 3-month return of -6.7% looks too negative for April alone. The 3 months to end-April run from end-January, and January ended at about 2822 against about 2648 at the end of April. That is -6.2% on price, so the figure is plausible.

The month is April 2018.
